rows.description: A child hears that someone is quiet and fond of books and says he must be a librarian, forgetting how many more farmers there are. The story outweighs the numbers.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager sure that a rare event happened because a report seemed reliable ignores how uncommon the event is. Vivid details beat plain frequency.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student fears a rare disease after a positive screening result, not realising that most positives for rare conditions are false alarms. Numbers need context.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A careful thinker begins with how common something is in general, then adjusts up or down for the specific evidence, and asks a professional to explain results.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A teenager thinks it more likely that a quiet friend is a shy artist who writes poems than simply an artist. Adding details makes a story feel truer though it becomes less probable.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student finds a detailed success story more believable than a simple one, though every added detail is one more thing that must go right.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A colleague notices a persuasive pitch full of specific steps and reminds the team each extra step lowers the chance of everything working together.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child notices that the days he wears his red shirt are the days his team wins and decides the shirt causes it. Things that happen together seem linked.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager sees that students who take tuition score higher and concludes tuition is the cause, missing that motivated or better-off students do both.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student reads that coffee drinkers live longer and starts believing coffee is the reason. Hidden third factors, or reversed direction, often explain links.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
